02 — About

The hand behind the pixels.

I'm Micheal Monday, working under MikemorArt — a graphite portrait artist based in Abuja, Nigeria.

I turn everyday faces into striking pieces of art, capturing not just likeness but the mood and personality behind every subject. What started as a passion has grown into a craft I take seriously: every piece is hand-drawn in graphite pencil, built layer by layer, until it feels alive on paper.

No shortcuts, no filters doing the work for me — just skill, patience, and an eye for detail. I work with clients across Nigeria and beyond, creating custom portraits for personal keepsakes, gifts, and brand projects.

If you've got a face worth immortalizing, I've got the hands for it.

03 — Process

How a portrait gets built.

Every commission moves through the same four stages — edit the copy to match how you actually work.

i. Reference & brief You send photos and tell me the mood you want — warm, formal, playful, dramatic. We agree on crop and format.
ii. Sketch pass A rough layout to lock proportions and expression before any rendering begins. You approve before I go further.
iii. Layer & render The bulk of the work — building form, light, and texture in graphite, layer by layer, until the piece feels alive.
iv. Finishing & delivery Final detail pass and fixative seal, then delivery in person (Abuja) or securely packaged for shipping.
